frequency_question: How often do major partisan election reform bills pass the U.S. Senate when subject to procedural friction under divided or narrow-margin control?
membership_rule: Federal bills introduced and passed in one chamber dealing with voter eligibility, registration, or election administration that faced procedural friction (such as the filibuster) in the U.S. Senate.

cases.name: John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act

coverage_note: 4 major omnibus federal election integrity or reform bills tracked since 1993.
known_gaps: Minor technical corrections bills are excluded as they do not face the same structural friction.
skeleton: Major federal electoral procedure bills considered in the U.S. Senate under modern filibuster rules requiring 60 votes.
validity_reason: Filibuster and Senate rules regarding electoral legislation remain stable within this horizon.
